claims.text: Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles exhibit atomic-scale chemical heterogeneity.
Atomic-scale chemical heterogeneity governs the premelting and melting behavior of Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu nanoparticles.
Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu nanoparticles undergo spatially heterogeneous melting transitions.
Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu nanoparticles have a broader melting range than homogeneous single-metal nanoparticles.
The initial particles are solid Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
Inert or vacuum conditions avoid oxidation during heating.
Atomic-scale chemical heterogeneity arises from the complex multielement composition.
Configurational disorder produces local variations in bonding.
Configurational disorder produces local variations in surface energy.
Local variations in bonding and surface energy cause different regions of a nanoparticle to begin melting at different temperatures.
High-entropy-alloy nanoparticles will show localized, sequential melting events.
Pure nickel or cobalt nanoparticles of comparable size show a relatively sharp and spatially uniform melting transition.
The proposed mechanism applies to equiatomic or near-equiatomic high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles between approximately 5 and 50 nm under oxidation-free conditions.
The proposed mechanism may not apply to larger particles.
The proposed mechanism may not apply to alloys that develop distinct phase segregation.
